summary: SL-087 turned the failed-folder record into a flat, path-sorted, uncapped list of rows, each with a kind label and a plain or Windows-message reason. To make the kind come from the engine, UnreadableFolder became a sealed record class with an internal constructor and a public Kind (NothingListed or ListedPartway), stamped in Scanner.FolderDone from ChildCount > 0. The row logic sits in one WPF-free file, src/FsAnalyser.App/UnreadableRows.cs, linked into Core.Tests, with two twinned architecture rules. The final state is 478 tests green, rules-parity AGREE, and all seven Done-when items met. Two code-review minors are still open: O-022, a rule that misses the repo's three-line ternary layout, and O-023, a sort that splits a folder from its descendants when a sibling differs only in case. The loop ran the risk spike, critique, code review and validate twice each.

payload.reason: Reflection written from the full slice record. O-022 and O-023 are open obligations aimed at build-slice and do not block this reflection, so they are not raised again as candidates.
payload.summary: SL-087 turned the failed-folder record into a flat, path-sorted, uncapped list of rows, each with a kind label and a plain or Windows-message reason. To make the kind come from the engine, UnreadableFolder became a sealed record class with an internal constructor and a public Kind (NothingListed or ListedPartway), stamped in Scanner.FolderDone from ChildCount > 0. The row logic sits in one WPF-free file, src/FsAnalyser.App/UnreadableRows.cs, linked into Core.Tests, with two twinned architecture rules. The final state is 478 tests green, rules-parity AGREE, and all seven Done-when items met. Two code-review minors are still open: O-022, a rule that misses the repo's three-line ternary layout, and O-023, a sort that splits a folder from its descendants when a sibling differs only in case. The loop ran the risk spike, critique, code review and validate twice each.
payload.estimate_error: Size (medium, about 8 files, one engine line) was right and the tier held, but the risk was read in the wrong place. The epic framed this as display text, and most tests went to the reason text and phrase tables. The two defects that survived review both lived elsewhere. One was in the sort tie-break. The other was in the twinned architecture rule that Done-when #7 forced, where the xUnit twin and the fitness engine match differently. The public engine record that Done-when #3 forced was the third hazard; the design marked it expensive to reverse. The next slice with a Done-when that asks for an architecture rule or a change to a public Core record should be sized as engine-and-rules work, not as a view slice. It should also budget for the parity, harness and RuleCases verification, which took about as many build commands as the feature itself.
what_went_wrong: The slice opened on a promise the public engine could not keep. Done-when #3 says the kind is 'taken from the engine's own record', and the epic verdict U-103 ('held') had been measured through scratch counters. The risk spike returned a no-go: UnreadableFolder was (Entry, Win32Error) only. The override text that let the loop proceed talked about working out each row's 'kind' from the error code with a fixed table. That conflates the phrase table (#4) with the opened/partway kind (#3), and the design correctly did not follow it. The outcome was a public-contract change inside a slice framed as display work.

The critique halted with 10 findings, 3 of them majors. One was the design's own test plan contradicting itself (the 1..16000 'contains its decimal number' sweep versus phrases that carry no number, failing on 23 codes). A second was a public enum name asserting a fact the engine does not know. A third was an invariant held by a regex instead of by the type. A single-designer design had no disagreement on record, and the critique-review was skipped by sizing, so all 10 findings were disposed with no second reader.

Code review ran twice and its round-2 minors were left 'owed to build-slice', but no build round followed. Validate #1 halted 'partial' only on those two items after a full real-contact round (four real scans, exe republish, S-007, rules harness). Validate #2 then passed with O-022 and O-023 still open. The slice finishes with a known-false doc comment ('a folder comes straight before everything under it') and a rule blind to the repo's usual layout.

rules-parity reported AGREE while the two rule engines behaved differently. The parity script compares pattern text, but the xUnit twin matches one line at a time (ArchitectureRulesTests.cs:234-239) and fitness matches the whole file. Plant F29 was a one-line ternary, so the harness recorded AS-RECORDED and hid the gap. Code review found it by planting the three-line form: the Fact passed 1/1 while fitness fired at MainWindow.xaml.cs:502.

ComparePaths was declared a 'total order, so descendants stay directly under their folder'. The tie-break is applied to whole paths, so [readme\x, README\y, readme, README] sorts to README | readme | readme\x | README\y. The C-005 test fed only leaf paths under C:\cs and passed. Total order and subtree contiguity were treated as the same property.

The engine materialised the design's two architecture_rules as SETTLED entries at the end of fitness.yaml, with no (?m), no including_comments and no xUnit twin. The build had to move them above the first '# settled by' marker. The spike had listed exactly these constraints, and the mechanism that writes the rules did not carry them.

The shipped exe cannot be asked what a row says. --report serialises only the tab header and the list layout (WindowReport.cs:164-168). Validation therefore compiled UnreadableRows.cs into a scratch console against the built Core, so the text of the real ListedPartway and non-5 phrase rows was never read from the running window. No real ListedPartway folder occurred on this PC in four real scans; that label has only been seen through the ScanFailingPartway failpoint.

The 'N' now differs by surface. The tab header counts distinct rows, while the largest-files and kinds captions still count raw result.Unreadable.Count. The dedup is defensive, because FolderDone never records an entry twice today. Nobody inventoried the other consumers of Unreadable.Count when the header's meaning changed.

learned.lesson: A twinned rule has two matchers with different semantics: the xUnit twin runs each pattern per line (File.ReadAllLines) and fitness runs it over the whole file. rules-parity only compares pattern text, so it cannot see the difference. Any must_not_match pattern that needs a token from a second line (the repo's ternary layout puts ':' on the next line, 24 App lines) passes dotnet test and fires only in fitness. Design every new pattern so it holds on a single line, and add a plant written in the repo's real multi-line layout with expected fire/fire, not only a one-line plant.
learned.evidence: R2-m1: with a three-line plant in MainWindow.xaml.cs the Fact passed 1/1 and fitness reported a violation at :502. rules-parity said 'AGREE 14 facts <- 18 twinned entries'. F29 is one-line and reported AS-RECORDED.

learned.lesson: For any flat list of paths that reuses UnreadableRows.ComparePaths, a total order does not keep a folder next to its descendants when siblings differ only in case, because the ordinal tie-break is applied to whole paths, not per component. A sort test that feeds only leaf paths cannot detect this. Include a folder, its child and a case-variant sibling: [readme\x, README\y, readme, README] should sort to README, README\y, readme, readme\x.
learned.evidence: R2-m2 measured the current output as README | readme | readme\x | README\y. The C-005 test (UnreadableRowsTests.cs:107-118) uses leaves only and passes. O-023 is still open.

learned.lesson: Epic verdicts of the form 'the engine records X' (U-097, U-102, U-103) were measured through scratch hooks, reflection into internals, or counters on net9 scratch copies. They did not establish that the public ScanResult exposes X. The next slice that consumes ScanResult.Unreadable or another engine record should check the public shape at HEAD first, from an assembly that is not a Core friend (only FsAnalyser.Core.Tests has InternalsVisibleTo), before trusting a 'held' verdict.
learned.evidence: The spike 'unreadable-kind-is-public-explicit-member' returned no-go against U-103 'Held'. U-102 recorded 'LastAccessAsked/LastAccessKept are internal to Core (read by reflection)'. The fix was a public-contract change (UnreadableFolder.Kind).

learned.lesson: UnreadableFolder.Kind is stamped as ChildCount(folder) > 0, and the same formula is still copied in FolderTreeNode.Note (FolderTreeNode.cs:86-90) and TopLevelTracker.cs:96. The tree also says 'could not be read in full' where the list says 'only partly read'. NothingListed conflates a refused open with an open that failed before the first entry. Any change to the stamp must move the tree, the top-level rows and the list in one slice; changing only one makes the surfaces disagree about the same folder.
learned.evidence: Build decisions: M2 fallback (rename to NothingListed plus a documented limit) and m1 deferred. The 28 code-363 rows under %TEMP%\fsa-guard-tests read 'could not be opened' with the failing phase unmeasured.

learned.lesson: A slice that declares architecture_rules should expect the engine to append them as settled entries with no twin. The build must move them above the first '# settled by' marker in .taad/fitness.yaml and add the (?m) prefix, including_comments: true, an xUnit Fact with identical patterns, and plant rows. The verification set is eng/rules-parity.ps1, harness.py --scenario all (59 rows now, F27-F29 added) and tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 run one -Case at a time (-Case is mandatory). With including_comments: true, doc comments in the guarded file cannot name the forbidden APIs, and even the pattern's own literal spelling had to be obscured ('(Dll|Library)Import').
learned.evidence: Build deviations: rules were appended settled with no (?m) or including_comments; the interop pattern was respelled; a RuleCases run without -Case failed.

learned.lesson: A code-review finding disposed 'accepted-pending, owed to build-slice' does not send the slice back to build. It waits as an open obligation, and validate halts 'partial' on it. Either route such minors to a build round straight away, or record them as deferred, or validate spends a full real-contact round rediscovering what review already said.
learned.evidence: O-022 and O-023 stayed open. Validate #1 halted on them after four real scans, an exe republish and S-007, and validate #2 passed without the fixes.

learned.lesson: The --report schema serialises only the Unreadable tab header and the list's layout, not row text. A slice that changes what a row says cannot have that text read from the shipped exe. Validation compiles the App source file into a scratch console instead. If the next slice changes list wording, either extend WindowReport to include a bounded sample of row text or accept that the window is checked by header count only.
learned.evidence: Validate 'not reached': row text inside the shipped window. WindowReport.cs:164-168 serialises UnreadableList only as actualHeight/inView/fullRows.

learned.lesson: Test scratch on this PC leaks failed folders that later real scans pick up as genuine misses. A scan of %TEMP% recorded 43 rows: 28 x code 363 and 2 x 1920 from fsa-guard-tests cloud placeholders, and 13 x code 5 from fsa-window-cases. Earlier epic measurements were polluted the same way (U-110: 30 of 682 C: failed rows were test-leftover cloud/0x123 dirs; U-111: code 363 on 28 rows, all in test fixtures). Any slice that validates against a real C: or %TEMP% scan must subtract these paths or clean them first.
learned.evidence: Build and validate scans of %TEMP% (43 rows). U-110 and U-111 verdict text.

learned.lesson: Dedup by Entry and the header counting 'distinct rows' are defensive: Scanner.FolderDone appends once per folder, so the record never holds duplicates today. The header changed to rows.Count while the largest-files and kinds captions still use result.Unreadable.Count. If a later slice touches those captions, point them at the same count, or drop the dedup and the split goes away. Grep every reader of Unreadable.Count when the meaning of an 'N' changes.
learned.evidence: Build left-open: 'the captions still count raw record entries ... differ only if the engine ever records an entry twice, which FolderDone does not today.'

learned.lesson: For a slice with a rules Done-when, expect the halts and reruns to come from the rules and the public record, not from the feature text. Here the spike, critique, code review and validate each ran twice, yet the reason-text tables and 74 targeted tests passed on the first design. The 22-code phrase table, the 1..16000 sweep and the 10,050-entry sort all went green with one test typo.
learned.evidence: Rework: risk-spike, critique, code-review and validate-slice each ran 2 times. The only first-run test failure was a verbatim-string typo. All surviving defects were the rule pattern (O-022) and the sort tie-break (O-023).

missed.what: Rule 2's must_not_match pattern `\?\s*UnreadableKind\.(NothingListed|ListedPartway)\s*:` needs the ':' on the same line as the '?'. The xUnit twin matches one line at a time, and the repo writes ternaries as three lines. The spike's own evidence said the twin matches line by line. The critique's M3 attacked this rule's evasion forms (switch, if/else, target-typed new) but never asked whether the twin sees the repo's own ternary layout, or whether the F29 plant was one-line. To be catchable: 'run each pattern against a three-line ternary through both the twin and fitness'. rules-parity also cannot see it.
missed.caught_by: code-review round 2 (R2-m1), by planting the three-line form in MainWindow.xaml.cs; the Fact passed while fitness fired

missed.what: The design's key decision says the path order is total, so 'descendants stay directly under their folder', with an ordinal tie-break on full paths. A whole-path tie-break does not keep a folder's descendants contiguous when a sibling differs from the folder only in case. The critique reviewed the sort (m7, Explorer numeric order) but did not ask what happens to a folder's children when its sibling differs only in case. To be catchable: 'sort [readme\x, README\y, readme, README] and check contiguity'.
missed.caught_by: code-review (filed as m2 / R2-m2, confirmed by compiling a copy of ComparePaths)

missed.what: The design changed the tab header's N from Unreadable.Count to rows.Count (distinct rows) and only asked whether --report or WindowCases read the count. It did not inventory the other readers of result.Unreadable.Count: the largest-files and kinds captions still count raw record entries. To be catchable: 'grep all consumers of Unreadable.Count when the header's meaning changes'.
missed.caught_by: build, noted as a left-open item and not fixed

unknowns: Do the 28 real code-363 cloud-placeholder rows under %TEMP%\fsa-guard-tests fail at the open or at the first directory query? That decides whether 'could not be opened' is true for them, and it needs the opt-in CfProvider rig (Trait Cloud=CF-SYNC-ROOT) with the provider stopped.

Does FormatMessage with langId 0 give the user's display language, or the thread or regional locale? This PC is en-US display, en-IN regional and en-US install, so every lookup resolves to en-US and Done-when #5's language clause has never been able to fail. It needs a machine whose display language differs from its regional format and install language.

Is 'only partly read' reachable on local drives at all? Four real scans (C:\ProgramData, %TEMP%, and two stopped scans) produced zero ListedPartway rows, which matches U-098's 0 partly-listed. Is the label effectively a network-share feature, and does the opt-in SmbRig loopback rig produce one through UnreadableRows.Build?
Does any other twinned rule in fitness.yaml carry a pattern that spans a line break and so passes its xUnit Fact but fires only in fitness? rules-parity compares pattern text only, so it cannot say.

Do the plain-phrase codes other than 5 (32/33 sharing and lock violations, the network and share family including 59 and 64) show the right phrase from a real scan? They have only been seen through the unit table.

candidates.title: Stamp UnreadableKind from the reader's open-versus-list phase, and make the tree and top-level rows read the stamped Kind
candidates.why: M2 and m1 were deferred by decision, not fixed. NothingListed currently means 'no entry was listed', so a folder that opened and then failed before its first entry reads 'could not be opened'. Start by measuring the 28 real code-363 rows with the CfProvider rig. Then carry an 'opened' bit out of DirectoryReader's ReadOutcome to Scanner.FolderDone, and switch FolderTreeNode.Note (:86-90) and TopLevelTracker (:96) to read UnreadableFolder.Kind. Align the tree's 'could not be read in full' with the list's 'only partly read'. The three surfaces must change together, or they will disagree about the same folder.

candidates.title: Check the shipped Unreadable list's row text end to end, including a real partly-read row and the network-phrase codes
candidates.why: Validation could not reach three things: row text in the running exe (--report serialises only the header and layout), any real ListedPartway folder, and the 32/33 and network-family phrases from a real scan. The opt-in SmbRig loopback rig (U-103 shape) can produce a real 59/64 partway record. Run it through UnreadableRows.Build, and either add a bounded sample of row Text to WindowReport or add a WindowCases check so the shipped window is what gets read.

candidates.title: Stop the test scripts leaking failed folders into %TEMP% and C:
candidates.why: A real scan of %TEMP% found 43 failed folders left by earlier runs: fsa-guard-tests cloud placeholders (28 x 363, 2 x 1920) and fsa-window-cases denied folders (13 x 5). The same pollution appeared in U-110 (30 of 682 C: rows) and U-111, so real-scan counts on this PC are inflated by our own fixtures, and U-098-style figures cannot be trusted. Make the fixtures clean up after themselves (the C-005 scratch-folder hygiene case), including when a test aborts, and check that a clean %TEMP% scan records none.
